data.name: Chaitranjan
data.gender_notes: Chaitranjan is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chaitra refers to the first month of Hindu calendar and Jana means 'born'. Thus, Chaitranjan signifies 'the reflection of the moon during the first month of Hindu calendar'. The name Chaitranjan carries the meaning “Moon's Reflection” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chaitranjan usually hope their child will grow to embody moon's reflection and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of growth and renewal, reflecting the divine light within.
data.etymology: Chaitranjan belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon's Reflection.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chaitranjan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Chaitranjan carries a deep cultural significance as it is derived from ancient Hindu traditions. This name reflects the connection to the rural yearly cycles and the agricultural community. The name also suggests a sense of being rooted in one's heritage, with its strong link to the Indian lunisolar calendar.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Chaitranjan could represent the divine illumination during the first month of the Hindu calendar. It symbolizes new beginnings and the renewal of life. The connection to the moon in this name can represent the inner reflection and self-awareness, allowing for greater self-understanding and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chaitra signifies the arrival of spring, renewal, and new beginnings. The suffix 'Njan' in Malayalam language means 'I'. Thus, Chaitranjan symbolizes the individual embracing the joy and renewal of spring within oneself.

vedic_reference.note: Not from any scriptures, but a common name

historical_references.reference: Chaitra Navratri is a major Hindu festival celebrated in Chaitra month (March-April) in honor of the nine goddesses. This festival marks the beginning of new year for many Hindus. The name 'Chaitra' is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Chaitra' which means 'bright', 'shining', 'dawn'.
historical_references.context: Hindu festival and new year for some Hindus

historical_references.reference: Chaitanyamaharaj (1495-1534 CE), a renowned Hindu saint, philosopher and poet, was also known as Chaitanya or Chaitranjan. He is considered the pioneer of the Bhakti movement in Bengal, and is regarded as an incarnation of Lord Krishna. He popularized the chanting of Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare, Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare.
historical_references.context: Renowned Hindu saint, philosopher, and poet
